title: Client Friction Minimization for Hosted Streaming + Tooling
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic PRD-style working note focused on reducing client-side friction for teams integrating Redwood Hosted Streaming with first-class tool-calls and structured output. Goal: make it easy for product engineers to adopt streaming + tools with minimal custom client-side plumbing, defendable latency SLOs, reliable resume semantics, and clear migration paths for typed schemas.

Scope (what this covers):
- SDK ergonomics for partial/streamed structured responses (frames, deltas, typed events)
- Tool call handshake semantics when used over streaming transports (HTTP/2, websockets, server-sent events)
- Backpressure and client-driven deadline/priority hints for low-latency paths
- Mobile and low-bandwidth client strategies (snapshots, compact frames, progressive fidelity)
- Migration & schema evolution for typed tool outputs (versioning, backwards compatibility checks)
- Observability hooks and minimal telemetry surface for client teams to diagnose integration issues

Not in scope (deferred):
- Server-side routing policies (handled by runtime product PRDs)
- Detailed server implementation plans (implementation doc to follow)

High-level requirements:
1) Minimal integration surface: client should be able to wire streaming responses and tool calls using <=3 API calls in the SDK (open session, receive frames/calls, acknowledge/complete).
2) Latency-safe fast-path: SDK surfaces a fast-path for token-forwarding and action hygenics where tool call negotiation does not add >15ms avg overhead in regional deployments under normal loads.
3) Resume & determinism: partial-response sessions must support resumability using small checkpoints (<=1KB snapshot tokens) without replaying entire context.
4) Typed outputs: SDK exposes typed bindings (JSON Schema / OpenAPI-lite) to validate tool payloads at the boundary and produce clear developer errors when contracts diverge.
5) Graceful degradation: when streaming or tool backends are unavailable, SDK provides deterministic fallbacks: (a) switch to non-streaming blocking call, or (b) return best-effort partial results flagged to the app.
6) Low-bandwidth/mobile: SDK can opt into compact framing and progressive fidelity modes that prioritize short summaries then full payloads.

Design notes and recommended APIs (sketch):
- Connection model:
  * openSession(opts) -> SessionHandle (WebSocket/HTTP2 duplex or SSE-based)
  * sendPrompt(session, prompt, callHints) -> requestId
  * onFrame(session, callback(frame)) -> frames: {type: "token", "partial_json", "action_request", "checkpoint", "meta"}
  * ackFrame(session, frameId, disposition) // optional for at-least-once semantics

- Frame types (compact):
  * token: raw text tokens for streaming UI (small payloads for low-latency render)
  * partial_json: incremental JSON patch or path/value pairs for structured outputs
  * action_request: tool call descriptor {tool_id, input, schema_version, request_id}
  * checkpoint: small opaque resume token + cursor position
  * meta: progress markers, estimated remaining tokens

- Tool handshake flow (sketch):
  1) model emits action_request frame referencing a declared tool id and schema_version.
  2) SDK validates tool id against client-registered tool table and attempts local execution or remote proxy execution.
  3) SDK responds with action_response frame {request_id, status: accept|decline|defer, result?: payload, error?: message}.
  4) If accepted, server continues generation with tool result injected. If declined, model receives a structured decline token and may fallback.

- Backpressure and priorities:
  * Client can send budget hints with sendPrompt: {latency_target_ms, cost_priority (low|med|high)}. Server uses hints to select batching and fallback policies.
  * Session-level flow control: SDK exposes a window size (frames outstanding). When window is full, SDK automatically pauses read buffer + exposes onBackpressure callback so apps can show degraded UI.

- Resume semantics:
  * Checkpoint frames carry a compact opaque token representing KVcache and prompt cursor (size target <=1KB).
  * Resume API: resumeSession(session, checkpointToken) -> stream picks up from nearest consistent model variant.
  * If model variant no longer available, server responds with resume_mismatch frame and SDK offers fallback options (full replay, fallback finalization).

- Typed schema & client validation:
  * Tool descriptors register an expected schema (JSON Schema subset) at client init: registerTool({id, name, schema, handler}).
  * SDK performs lightweight validation on incoming action_request and partial_json frames: if mismatch -> emit client_warning and attach instrumentation.
  * Migration: schema_version is a semantic string; server can emit schema_diff frames to highlight non-breaking vs breaking changes.

- Mobile & low-bandwidth modes:
  * compactFrames: boolean that minimizes verbose keys and uses integer codes for frame types + compressed base64 payloads.
  * fidelityLevels: summary|expandable|full. Start at summary, SDK exposes fetchFull(requestId) to request full payload when user taps.
  * offline snapshots: SDK can persist last checkpoint + partial_json fragments to local storage for offline resume UX.

Observability / debugging primitives:
- Per-session trace id surfaced on every frame.
- Client-side counters: frames_received, frames_acknowledged, action_calls_initiated, schema_mismatches (incremental).
- Suggested telemetry export: minimal event set to Redwood Console (opt-in): {session_id, request_id, client_sdk_version, frames_late_pct, resume_fail_count}.

Acceptance criteria (how we’ll know this is successful):
- Developer integration time: measured median time from SDK install to first successful tool-call integration <= 90 minutes (internal samples).
- Latency: in 95th percentile under normal load, additional tool-call handshake overhead <= 25ms in regional deployment for websocket trunks.
- Resume effectiveness: >= 98% of resumed sessions recover without requiring full history replay in controlled tests.
- Schema compatibility: SDK should detect and surface breaking schema changes in preflight checks with at least one meaningful warning in dev mode for 100% of registered tools during canary rollout.
- Mobile data: compactFrames mode must reduce payload size by >= 40% relative to verbose framing in our synthetic mobile trace.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should SDK make ackFrame required for strict at-least-once semantics? Requires heavier developer checks vs. best-effort latency. Suggest opt-in ack mode for mission-critical clients.
- How aggressively do we push schema validation on the client vs. server? Client validation catches consumer issues earlier but duplicates work; propose lightweight shallow validation client-side + deep validation server-side.
- Version negotiation for resume tokens: how to handle KV cache drift across model improvements? Proposal: include model_variant_id in checkpoint and fallback to replay when variant mismatch occurs.
- Do we support signed/resumable tokens for air-gapped/private deployments? Likely necessary for Private customers; include HMAC-signed tokens when deployment mode==private.

Developer experience examples (playful sketches):
- Minimal React hook (pseudo):
  const session = await openSession({auth, region: 'us-west'});
  const r = sendPrompt(session, "Summarize doc:", {latency_target_ms: 200});
  onFrame(session, (f) => { if(f.type === 'partial_json') setState(patch(f.payload)); if(f.type === 'action_request') handleToolRequest(f); });

- Tool registration:
  registerTool({id: 'search-v1', name: 'DocSearch', schema: {type: 'object', properties: {query: {type: 'string'}}}});

Implementation plan (next steps):
1) Ship SDK v0.1 with read-only frames and token + action_request support (no ack or resume). Target: Q1 2026 experimental release.
2) Iteration v0.2: add checkpoints, compact framing, and client-side schema validation (Q2 2026).
3) Beta: ack mode, resume tokens signed for private deployments, telemetry integration with Console (pilot customers) (Q3 2026).
4) Finalize API ergonomics and docs, create migration guide for customers moving from blocking tool calls to streaming tool handshake (Q4 2026).

Risks & mitigations:
- Complexity in client SDKs across languages (JS, mobile native): mitigate by focusing on a minimal canonical JS SDK first + language-neutral framing spec.
- Backwards compatibility with older hosted endpoints: design server to support fallback to non-streaming path when clients signal legacy flag.
- Network middleboxes interfering with websockets/HTTP2: provide SSE fallback and clear diagnostics in SDK.

Appendix: quick checklist for integration guides (to include in final docs):
- Quickstart: 10-minute sample using openSession/sendPrompt/onFrame
- Tool migration guide: how to register tools + handle versioned schemas
- Debugging: list of common frames and what they mean, how to interpret resume_mismatch
- Bandwidth tuning: when to enable compactFrames / fidelityLevels
- Canonical error codes and remediation steps (client-side)

Notes to reviewers (things I want feedback on):
- Are the frame types expressive enough to cover typical structured-output workloads (tables, json-lists, nested objects)?
- Does the proposed checkpoint size target (<1KB) strike the right balance? Too small may lose KVcache fidelity.
- Tradeoffs around mandatory acks: would like feedback from SRE/serving-runtime on feasibility and cost.

Status: draft, seeking product + serving-runtime + SDK leads to align on the framing spec and resume semantics before moving to an implementation RFC.

-- Asha
